A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching content across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original behavioral evaluations of 48 language models and localization and ablation experiments involving 20 models.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical investigations and adds SNLI evaluations, reasoning-task ablations on 13 models, and analyses comparing original and synthetic localizer stimuli.

M1.justification: The four localizer suites, last-token activation measurements, simple and conjunctive localization statistics, 1% selection cap, least-active controls, and zero ablations are retained. Clarified notation and descriptions do not establish a changed localization algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 retains the ToM, pragmatics, and BLiMP evaluations while adding SNLI natural language inference, entity tracking, verbal analogies, and story analogies. These substantially broaden the capabilities evaluated beyond the original task coverage.

E2.justification: The behavioral and localization model rosters and the intact-model and least-active ablation comparisons remain unchanged. The 13 models used for the added reasoning tests come from the existing roster; no competing localization method is introduced.

E3.justification: The general-language control changes from BLiMP alone to aggregated BLiMP and SNLI performance in behavioral and ablation analyses. Added protocols include 670-item SNLI and entity-tracking samples, multiple-choice reasoning evaluations on 13 models, and matched original/synthetic samples for two-component PCA.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds PCA comparisons testing whether synthetic localizers resemble their source stimuli. Appendix D.1 adds reasoning-task ablations testing whether localized effects extend to general cognitive skills. Neither investigation appears in v1; the existing localization cross-validation and method-comparison analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Appendix A.5 specifies Lambert’s z-score method for calculating LOO-CV comparison p-values. Both versions already report posterior means, 95% credible intervals, and significance tests; no increase in repeated runs or new seed-reporting practice is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds SNLI, reasoning-task, and PCA findings and updates regression estimates and Table 5. With the expanded linguistic control, the behavioral P3 ELPD comparison changes from -16.8 to -16.1, and GameBeliefs’ P3.1 interval changes from [-0.06, 0.81] to [0.06, 0.64]. New ablations show substantial entity-tracking effects. These are added or revised results under changed controls, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of localizer suites and simple/conjunctive selection statistics remain substantively unchanged. Appendix A.5 explains the existing regression and cross-validation analyses without introducing new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the Discussion retains the same five contributions and suggestive support for shared ToM/pragmatic mechanisms. Added experiments do not redefine the central functional-integration claim.

C2.justification: Sections 3.5 and 4 and Appendix D.1 introduce shared entity tracking and broader cognitive abilities as substantive explanations for the observed overlap, qualifying its social interpretation. Appendix C.3 explains the HumanDescr stimulus mismatch, and the Limitations add concerns about pragmatics-benchmark precision and diversity.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the redacted code/data reference with a repository address. It also documents SNLI sampling and scoring, the PCA embedding model and sampling procedure, and reasoning-task prompts and model selection. Existing localization implementation and stimulus-generation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 expands cognitive-science framing with Austin, Goodman et al., and Goodman and Frank, and adds references supporting SNLI, entity tracking, analogies, and sentence embeddings. Its principal positioning relative to earlier functional-localization research remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction is reorganized around an explicit Related Work & Contributions heading, terminology and procedural explanations are clarified, and statistical exposition is expanded. The overall narrative structure and substantial portions of the prose are retained.

P2.justification: The original benchmark Figures 5–6 are enlarged and split into Figures 5–8, and the ATOMS comparison becomes a full-page horizontal display. Figure 3 changes its illustrative model and linguistic-control labeling. New PCA and reasoning figures substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Broader linguistic and reasoning controls, synthetic-stimulus checks, clearer benchmark figures, and a concrete code/data pointer improve scrutiny and reproducibility. However, the added analyses leave the central social-specificity question unresolved: entity tracking is also strongly affected, and the global P3.2 contrast remains unsupported. The revision provides useful additional evidence and qualifications without resolving that central ambiguity.
